project.objective: Identify the parents of Cornelis van Noord (b. ~1828) of Zuid-Holland, Netherlands.

researcher_profile.narration_guidance: Write one clear sentence before each action and omit hedging phrases.

questions.question: Who was the mother of Cornelis van Noord (b. ~1828, Zuid-Holland)?
questions.rationale: The birth act names the mother but the OCR reading is uncertain; a ten-year marriage index from a different record names her differently.

items.rationale: The birth act should name both parents.
The ten-year marriage index should confirm the mother's name.
The marriage act itself names the groom's mother in full, where the index abbreviates; its duplicate copy and the marriage supplements' birth extract are independent readings of her name.
The mother's own death act names her as an adult, independently of either reading.
The population register lists the household with each member's name as the household gave it.
A sibling's birth act names the same mother in another clerk's hand.
The parents' own marriage act, civil from 1811 or a church entry before it, names the bride as she signed.
Cornelis's own death act names his parents, in the declarant's words rather than the 1828 clerk's.
The court's duplicate of the 1828 birth register is a separate copy in another hand, and may read the first letter the municipal copy blots.

log.notes: Found the 1828 birth act of Cornelis van Noord.
Found the ten-year marriage index entry for Cornelis van Noord.

The 1850 marriage act the index cites (act 31) is lost in both copies: the municipal register's images run from act 12 to act 61 with acts 13-48 absent, and the duplicate the court of first instance kept is missing the same quire. The 1850 marriage supplements (huwelijksbijlagen), which would hold the groom's birth extract copied in 1850, do not survive for that year. No other year carries a marriage of Cornelis van Noord.

No death act in Zuid-Holland 1828-1900 for a Jannetje, Fannetje or Tannetje married to a van Noord, under her own surname or her husband's. The 1851 death act of Cornelis's father names him as the widower of "[.]annetje van Noord": the first letter of her given name is blotted, as in the birth act, so it gives no independent reading.

The municipality's bevolkingsregister begins in 1850. It lists the father as a widower with no wife entered, and Cornelis, married that year, at his own address until he departs in 1853 "naar zee" (to sea). Neither entry names his mother.
No other birth to this couple in the municipality or its neighbours, 1820-1845: Cornelis was the only child registered.

No marriage of Pieter van Noord in the Zuid-Holland civil registers, kept from 1811, nor in the church marriage and banns registers (DTB) of the municipality and its neighbours before that, 1795-1811; the parents married at a place no record on file names.

No death act for Cornelis van Noord in Zuid-Holland or any other Dutch province, 1850-1950. He went to sea in 1853 (log_005) with no later address, and no Dutch register records his death, so no act exists that names his parents.

The duplicate of the 1828 birth register that the court of first instance kept does not survive: its 1828 volume is missing from the archive's holdings. Only the municipal copy is extant, and it blots the first letter of the mother's given name.

person_evidence.rationale: Birth act names Cornelis van Noord as the child; matches tree person I1 exactly.
Birth act names the mother; OCR reading uncertain (Jannetje [?]).
Ten-year marriage index names the mother as Fannetje van Noord; linked to same person I2.

conflicts.description: Mother's name: 'Jannetje [?] van Noord' (birth act OCR, first letter uncertain) vs. 'Fannetje van Noord' (ten-year marriage index). The user reads the birth act as 'Tannetje'.
conflicts.independence_analysis: The birth act (a_002) and the ten-year index (a_003) are independent records, but the index is a derivative abstract of a marriage act, and the act's own reading is not on file. The researcher's reading of the birth-act image is a third reading of the same entry as a_002, not an independent witness.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: Neither side outweighs the other: the birth act is the original but its first letter is unreadable, and the index is legible but derivative. Each reading is consistent with the other two letters; nothing on file breaks the tie.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: Cannot be settled from the birth act and the index alone. Decisive would be the marriage act itself, the mother's death act, the household in the population register, a sibling's birth act, or the parents' marriage act.
